blocks.text: Living in Canyon Heights, District of North Vancouver

Canyon Heights is in the District of North Vancouver, a hillside residential community on the west side of the District, toward the Capilano River canyons and the streets above Edgemont. It sits in the District, north of the City of North Vancouver. Capilano River Regional Park and the forested ravines are the local landscape.

Homes for sale in Canyon Heights are mainly houses on sloping, treed lots. Edgemont Village is the usual nearby shop street. Cleveland Dam and the regional park trails are a short trip, and the Grouse Mountain approach roads sit close by.

Buses on Capilano Road and the west-side District routes connect toward Marine Drive and the City of North Vancouver. Nearby public schools include those in the Canyon Heights and Capilano families. Check the SD44 school locator.

items.t: Canyon Heights is an Upper Capilano neighbourhood in the District of North Vancouver, on the Highland Boulevard corridor, west of Edgemont Village and east of the Capilano River. Nearby areas: Edgemont Village (east), Capilano Highlands (north), Forest Hills (north-east), Grouse Woods (north-west) and Queensdale (south-east).

Main streets: Highland Boulevard is the main road, carrying TransLink routes 246 and 232; Capilano Road on the west side carries routes 232 and 236 toward Grouse Mountain and south to Marine Drive and the Lions Gate Bridge; the Upper Levels Highway (Highway 1) is reached via Capilano Road or Edgemont Boulevard.

Transit anchors: route 246 (Downtown / Highland) runs via Marine Drive, Capilano Road, Ridgewood Drive, Edgemont Boulevard, Highland Boulevard and Montroyal Boulevard, with downtown-bound trips crossing the Lions Gate Bridge; route 232 (Grouse Mountain / Phibbs Exchange) runs via Highland Boulevard, Edgemont Boulevard and Capilano Road; route 236 runs on Capilano Road. There is no rapid transit and no condo node inside Canyon Heights.

blocks.text: Good to know about Canyon Heights condos

items.t: Highland Boulevard runs through two neighbourhoods, Canyon Heights and Edgemont. The condos on Connaught Crescent and the "EIGHT" duplex project at 3206 Highland Boulevard are in Edgemont, while the Canyon Heights stretch west of the village is detached houses only. A "Highland Boulevard condo" is almost never in Canyon Heights.

The flood data runs to 2100. The District's GeoWeb flood construction level data is modelled to a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m — a long-horizon number that can surprise a buyer pricing a river-side renovation off today's water levels.

Murdo Frazer's courts were restated in 2025. The Edgemont-area District park east of Canyon Heights carries 6 tennis courts and 6 pickleball courts in the District's Outdoor Sports Courts Optimization Strategy, approved July 21, 2025 — the shared amenity base for a neighbourhood with no strata amenity rooms.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Canyon Heights
Streets, schools and transit near Canyon Heights townhomes

items.t: There are no townhouses in Canyon Heights. The District's townhouses and condos are in its centres, Lynn Valley Town Centre, Lions Gate Village and Edgemont Village, all outside Canyon Heights; Edgemont is right next door.

Roads and transit: Highland Boulevard is the main road, with routes 246 and 232; Capilano Road on the west side has routes 232 and 236 to Grouse Mountain and south to Marine Drive and the Lions Gate Bridge; and the Upper Levels Highway is reached via Capilano Road or Edgemont Boulevard. Route 246 (Downtown / Highland) runs via Marine Drive, Capilano Road, Ridgewood Drive, Edgemont Boulevard, Highland Boulevard and Montroyal Boulevard, with downtown trips crossing the Lions Gate Bridge. The SeaBus from Lonsdale Quay reaches Waterfront Station in 12 minutes, every 15 minutes during the day. There's no rapid transit here.

Highlands Elementary, 3150 Colwood Drive, and Cleveland Elementary, 1255 Eldon Road, sit beside the area, and Handsworth Secondary is at 1033 Handsworth Road. SD44 has elementary (K–7) and secondary (8–12) schools only, with no middle tier, and catchments are address-based.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Canyon Heights

items.t: For strata homes in the nearby centres, read the Form B: it shows the monthly fee, amounts owing, approved special levies, the contingency reserve balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, budget, any rental disclosure and the latest depreciation report. The strata must provide it within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page.

Fee-simple homes (what Canyon Heights does have): Canyon Heights is in the District of North Vancouver, not the City of North Vancouver, so the City's Official Community Plan and zoning bylaw don't apply here.

District zoning and plan: District of North Vancouver Official Community Plan, Bylaw 7900 (including its Schedule B Development Permit Areas), and Zoning Bylaw 3210 — Section 525 (Bylaw 8799) sets the R1 minimum lot at 4,000 m² / 30 m width / 34 m depth and standard R2 at 660 m² / 18 m / 34 m, with modifiers R2(S1) at 335 m² / 10 m, R2(S2) at 1,100 m² / 24 m and R2(S3) at 4,000 m² / 30 m; an R2 principal building may include a secondary suite, and a coach house is a dwelling unit accessory to and detached from the principal dwelling unit.

items.t: The library is on the same boulevard, in the next neighbourhood. The Capilano Library, 3045 Highland Boulevard, is described by the North Vancouver District Public Library as "located in the heart of Edgemont Village" — east of Canyon Heights on the same street its townhouse searches run on, and the Delbrook Community Recreation Centre, 851 West Queens Road, south-east of the area, is the nearest full-service NVRC centre.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Canyon Heights
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Lots: detached houses zoned R1 or R2 (Zoning Bylaw 3210, Section 525) on the Highland Boulevard plateau between the Capilano River and the Mosquito and Mackay creek ravines. R1 lots must be at least 4,000 m², 30 m wide and 34 m deep; standard R2 lots 660 m², 18 m wide and 34 m deep, with variations R2(S1) at 335 m² and 10 m wide, R2(S2) at 1,100 m² and 24 m, and R2(S3) at 4,000 m² and 30 m. These are minimums, not actual lot sizes; check a specific lot's zone on the District's GeoWeb. A fee-simple lot has no strata, Form B or strata fees.

Suites as lot value: an R2 principal building may include a secondary suite, and a coach house is a dwelling unit accessory to and detached from the principal dwelling unit; since June 2024, District zoning permits a principal dwelling, a secondary suite and a coach house — three units total — on all single-family zoned properties within the Urban Containment Boundary. A suite or coach house is part of the house lot's ownership, not a separately saleable lot.

Serviced position, as the District states it: District single-family utility fees in 2026 include water at $932.80 and sewer/drainage at $1,255.60, with combined single-family utilities of $2,571 in 2026 — Canyon Heights' established lots sit inside that District serviced system on that wording.
Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any ALR rule.

Hazard-shaped land: District OCP Bylaw 7900, Schedule B sets seven Development Permit Areas, including Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside Protection, Wildfire Hazard, Creek Hazard and Slope Hazard — a Canyon Heights property can fall in one of these areas along the Capilano River side and on steeper ground, and the District publishes property-level GeoWeb reports, including modelled flood construction levels for a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m. Gross lot area is not buildable area here.

items.t: Municipality: District of North Vancouver, BC — Canyon Heights is an Upper Capilano neighbourhood on the Highland Boulevard corridor, west of Edgemont Village and east of the Capilano River.
Nearby areas: Edgemont Village (east), Capilano Highlands (north), Forest Hills (north-east), Grouse Woods (north-west, across the Capilano River side) and Queensdale (south-east).

Roads and transit: Highland Boulevard is the main road, carrying TransLink routes 246 and 232; Capilano Road on the west side carries routes 232 and 236 toward Grouse Mountain and south to Marine Drive and the Lions Gate Bridge; the Upper Levels Highway (Highway 1) is reached via Capilano Road or Edgemont Boulevard. Route 246 (Downtown / Highland) runs via Marine Drive, Capilano Road, Ridgewood Drive, Edgemont Boulevard, Highland Boulevard and Montroyal Boulevard, with downtown-bound trips crossing the Lions Gate Bridge.

Schools: SD44 catchments are address-based, with no middle tier (K–7 elementary, 8–12 secondary). Highlands Elementary, 3150 Colwood Drive, and Cleveland Elementary, 1255 Eldon Road, sit beside the area.

Parks and services: Capilano River Regional Park (Metro Vancouver), on the Capilano River west of the area, offers the Capilano Pacific Trail and the Coho Loop Trail; Mosquito Creek and Mackay Creek run through the Upper Capilano ravines east of the area. The Delbrook Community Recreation Centre, 851 West Queens Road, south-east of the area, is the nearest NVRC full-service centre; the Capilano Library, 3045 Highland Boulevard, is in Edgemont Village, east of the area. Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, North Vancouver, serves the North Shore.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Canyon Heights

items.t: OCP + zoning (District only): District of North Vancouver Official Community Plan, Bylaw 7900 (including its Schedule B Development Permit Areas), and Zoning Bylaw 3210, Section 525 (R1/R2 minimums in Sections 1–2). The City of North Vancouver's OCP 8400 / Zoning 6700 belong to the city only and are never imported here.

SSMUH / added units, as the District and Province state them: three units total (principal, secondary suite, coach house) are permitted on single-family zoned lots within the Urban Containment Boundary since June 2024. The District's GEOweb SSMUH classification shows non-exempt lots potentially allowing up to 3 units at 280 m² or less, up to 4 units above 280 m², and up to 6 units above 280 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit bus stop; provincial rules set 3 units on lots of 280 m² or smaller, 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on larger lots within 400 m of a prescribed bus stop. Verify the parcel's classification before pricing in unit potential.

What to do instead: confirm the zone and the District's GeoWeb property report for the lot (including hazard layers and the modelled flood construction level), then confirm servicing and any off-site works with the District before removing subjects.

Hazard development permits: OCP Bylaw 7900, Schedule B sets seven Development Permit Areas, including Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside Protection, Wildfire Hazard, Creek Hazard and Slope Hazard — whether a lot is in one is a District GeoWeb map check, and creek, slope and wildfire permit areas can add geotechnical and permit cost to a rebuild on river-side and steep lots.

Strata rules: check the Form B (fees, amounts owing, levies, contingency reserve balance and insurance; provided within 7 days for at most $35 plus 25¢ a page). Stratas with 5 or more lots need a depreciation report every 5 years, and at least 10% of the budget must go into the reserve. Rental bans are void (short-term rentals can still be limited), and the only valid age bylaw is 55 and older, with exemptions for a younger spouse or partner, caregivers, existing residents and some children, so a "45+" listing line isn't enforceable.

blocks.text: Good to know about Canyon Heights lots

items.t: The plateau is split by creeks, not just streets: Mosquito Creek and Mackay Creek run through the Upper Capilano ravines east of the area — District planning material describes Mosquito Creek as a "creekside natural area with well used trails" and MacKay Creek as a "creekside natural area with fish habitat" — so two lots on the same street can sit in different permit regimes.

The flood number is modelled to 2100, plus 0.6 m: the District's GeoWeb flood construction levels are modelled for a 2100 (2080s) horizon plus 0.6 m — a rebuild priced off today's water level alone is priced off the wrong document.

The retail is in the next neighbourhood, by plan: the District's OCP names Edgemont, immediately east, as one of its six Village Centres (with Lions Gate, Queensdale, Maplewood, Parkgate and Deep Cove) — Canyon Heights itself has no confirmed shopping centre or grocery store on a District source, and that is the plan working as written, not a gap about to be filled.

A direct downtown bus runs off the plateau: route 246 runs from Highland Boulevard via Edgemont and Capilano Road directly downtown over the Lions Gate Bridge, and route 232 links the area to Grouse Mountain and Phibbs Exchange — the car-light case for these lots rests on those two routes, not on a station.

No market figure exists to quote for this plateau: North Vancouver is outside SnapStats coverage entirely, so any Canyon Heights median, ratio or trend figure attributed to SnapStats anywhere should be treated as an error.

blocks.text: Duplexes and half duplexes in Canyon Heights
What a duplex looks like in Canyon Heights

items.t: The usual duplex form: in Canyon Heights, the realistic smaller option isn't a duplex complex. Since June 2024, District zoning has allowed a main home, a secondary suite and a coach house (three homes in total) on all single-family lots inside the Urban Containment Boundary, on one title. Existing duplexes are individual buildings on single lots, built under the zoning of their day. Check a specific duplex's title to see whether it's one lot, a strata or a subdivided pair.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect duplexes in Canyon Heights

items.t: Since June 2024, District zoning permits a principal dwelling, a secondary suite and a coach house — three units total — on all single-family zoned properties within the Urban Containment Boundary. A suite or coach house is part of the house lot's ownership — it cannot be bought separately. The District's GEOweb SSMUH classification shows non-exempt lots potentially allowing up to 3 units at 280 m² or less, up to 4 units above 280 m², and up to 6 units above 280 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop. SSMUH adds unit potential on one title; it does not by itself split a duplex into separately titled halves.
